stem: A diagram labels g and h for every free cell. Why is selecting the globally smallest labeled f over all cells NOT a valid replacement for an A* trace?
assumptions: Use the graph-search frontier convention demonstrated on physical pages 1121–1122.
The question concerns candidate eligibility, not the correctness of each numerical label on physical page 1135. Its inconsistent start g=1.0 label is not adopted as a rule.

options.text: The next expansion may be chosen from the explored set whenever one of its recorded f values is below all frontier values
A* selects among current discovered frontier entries; a final cost map does not show which cells are available at the current step
Every free cell with a printed heuristic is automatically a frontier entry, even before a route to it is generated
Once a cell receives any g label, that label is its final search cost and never needs a lower-cost update

solution.justification: A* minimizes f over its current frontier entries. A prelabelled map does not encode discovery, expansion or cost-update history and cannot replace the trace.

optionExplanations.o1: Eligibility depends on discovery and the current open set; a static table is not that changing set.
optionExplanations.o2: Knowing a heuristic is not the same as having generated a finite start-to-cell path and queued that state.
optionExplanations.o3: Search g values are best-known costs and may improve when a better path is found; a printed final map omits that history.
optionExplanations.o4: Already explored states are not chosen again merely because their old f is small; any reopening must follow the algorithm’s improved-path rule.

examTraps: A visible heuristic or final g label does not imply current frontier membership.
